<h>Lectio 1</h>
Incipit Epístola cathólica beáti Jacóbi Apóstoli
<r>Ias 1:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Jacóbus, Dei et Dómini nostri Jesu Christi servus, duódecim tríbubus, quæ sunt in dispersióne, salútem.
<n>2</n> Omne gáudium existimáte fratres mei, cum in tentatiónes várias incidéritis:
<n>3</n> Sciéntes quod probátio fídei vestræ patiéntiam operátur.
<n>4</n> Patiéntia autem opus perféctum habet: ut sitis perfécti et íntegri in nullo deficiéntes.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si oblítus fúero tui, allelúia, obliviscátur mei déxtera mea:
* Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Super flúmina Babylónis illic sédimus et flévimus, dum recordarémur tui, Sion.
<r>℟.</r> Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.
b.b477b85b1a:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the letter of St. James the Apostle
<r>Jas 1:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> James the servant of God, and of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
<n>2</n> My brethren, count it all joy, when you shall fall into diverse temptations;
<n>3</n> Knowing that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
<n>4</n> And patience hath a perfect work; that you may be perfect and entire, failing in nothing.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> If I forget thee, Alleluia, let my right hand forget me.
* If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> By the rivers of Babylon there we sat down and wept, when we remembered thee, O Zion.
<r>℟.</r> If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Ias 1:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Si quis autem vestrum índiget sapiéntia, póstulet a Deo, qui dat ómnibus affluénter, et non impróperat: et dábitur ei.
<n>6</n> Póstulet autem in fide nihil hǽsitans:
<n>6</n> Qui enim hǽsitat, símilis est flúctui maris, qui a vento movétur et circumfértur:
<n>7</n> Non ergo ǽstimet homo ille quod accípiat áliquid a Dómino.
<n>8</n> Vir duplex ánimo incónstans est in ómnibus viis suis.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Vidérunt te aquæ, Deus, vidérunt te aquæ, et timuérunt:
* Multitúdo sónitus aquárum vocem dedérunt nubes, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Illuxérunt coruscatiónes tuæ orbi terræ: vidit et commóta est terra.
<r>℟.</r> Multitúdo sónitus aquárum vocem dedérunt nubes, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

<r>Jas 1:5-8</r>

<n>6</n> But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.

<n>7</n> Therefore let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.

<n>11</n> For the sun rose with a burning heat, and parched the grass, and the flower thereof fell off, and the beauty of the shape thereof perished: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.
<n>12</n> Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.

b.2f3cbc6b3c:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.8224e6f1ab:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.92ec66205d:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Kaléndas Maii Luna vicésima prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Petri Canísii, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris atque Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui duodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii migrávit ad Dóminum.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ natális sancti Anthimi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, ob confessiónem Christi, martýrii glóriam obtruncatióne cápitis accépit. Secúta est quoque illum univérsa ferme gregis sui multitúdo; quorum álios Judex gládio obtruncári, álios conflagrári ígnibus, álios, navículis impósitos, pélago immérgi fecit.
<h>T</h>arsi, in Cilícia, sanctórum Castóris et Stéphani Mártyrum.
<h>B</h>onóniæ sancti Tertulliáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>B</h>ríxiæ sancti Theóphili Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Ægýpto sancti Theodóri Abbátis, qui fuit discípulus sancti Pachómii.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Joánnis Abbátis, qui pro cultu sacrárum Imáginum, sub Leóne Isáurico, plúrimum decertávit.
<h>T</h>arracóne, in Hispánia, beáti Petri Armengáudii, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum; qui, multa pro fidélibus rediméndis in Africa passus, tandem, in convéntu sanctæ Maríæ Pratórum, beáto fine quiévit.
<h>L</h>ucæ, in Túscia, beátæ Zitæ Vírginis, virtútum et miraculórum fama conspícuæ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.8f03cf1c5c:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 27th 2027, the 21st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>W</h>e keep the feast of the holy Priest and monk Egbert, a man of marvellous lowliness and self-denial, of whom mention has been made upon the 24th day of this present month of April.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyr Anthimus, Bishop of that see, who was beheaded for confessing Christ, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and so gained the glory of martyrdom. He was followed by almost all his flock, whereof by command of the judge some were slain with the sword, some burnt in fire, and some embarked upon ships and drowned in the sea.
<h>A</h>t Tarsus, in Cilicia, the holy martyrs Castor and Stephen. [St. Stephen was perhaps a Bishop.]
<h>A</h>t Bologna, [in the sixth century,] the holy Confessor Tertullian, Bishop of that see.
<h>A</h>t Brescia, [in the fifth century,] holy Theophilus, Bishop of that see.
<h>I</h>n Egypt, the holy monk Theodore (the Sanctified, Abbot from 348, death of St. Pachom of Tabenno, in Egypt. He lived from 314-April 27, 367), a disciple of holy Pachom.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Abbot John, [of the monastery of Cathares Hegumenos,] who contended much for the honouring of holy images under the Emperor Leo the Isaurian, [in the year 813, under Leo the Armenian. Leo the Isaurian reigned from 717-741.]
<h>A</h>t Taragona, the blessed Peter Armengal, of the Order of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Ransom for the Redemption of Captives. He suffered many things for the redemption of the faithful in Africa, and at length died a blessed death in the convent of St.-Mary-of-the-Meadows, [in the year 1304.]
<h>A</h>t Lucca, in Italy, [in the year 1278,] the blessed Virgin Zita, very famous for her graces and miracles.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.a37c4b84ad:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.04e4ee2fbd:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
